utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence to tell the truth still applies, and I think Mr. Hannis is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First I would like to have you take a look at tab 24 in your binder. This is document 65 ter number 01591. General, I believe this is a phone list that looks like some sort of internal phone list for, I think, your SUP in Pristina. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know what time-period this would be applicable to? Because I see the chief is listed as Djordje Keric, and I'm not sure when he was chief of your SUP. Do you know what year this would pertain to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really say what year with complete certainty, but I know that the Pristina -- chief of the Pristina Secretariat of the Interior, Djordje Keric, who is listed here, he served in that capacity from 1994 until 1997, but I'm not quite sure what time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And I see, I think, the fifth -- or the fourth name down is your name as department chief for the police department, and that was a position you held at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see to the far right of your name in the last column there's a UKF call-sign. I take it that's your radio call-sign, Grmija 1 -- or Grmija 3, I guess?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the -- that was my call-sign in a time-period, and after that it was changed, and I think it was Sitnica 101, if I'm not mistaken -- actually, I apologise. Let me just look at this. Yes, I think it was the way I just told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And that second call-sign you mentioned Sitnica 1. When was that used?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sitnica 101. I think that the call-signs were changed for everyone at a certain point in time and that everybody was assigned different call-signs, but again with the caveat if my memory serves me right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when that change took place, what year?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was sometime in 1996 or maybe 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Was that still in use in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me right, I don't think so. I don't think so, but let me tell you once again, I think it was changed at one point, as I've already indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what your radio call-sign was in 1998 and/or 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Sitnica 101.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Going down the column, number 26 the position is described as police station -- SM, which I think means police station, commander for, and then there's an acronym or an abbreviation which in English is translated as DiI. Can you tell me what that stands for, if you know? It's the position for V. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course that acronym -- this means the commander of the police station for duty and interventions, so this is probably the period before 1996 because I think that in 1996 that got changed. It was no longer Stanica milicija but policija, because the name of the organisation changed from milicija to policija, and I believe that it happened in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The last question on this document, number 28, two down from the column we were just looking at, there is an assistant commander named G. Djordjevic. Do you know who that was?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it was Goran Djordjevic, that's my assumption. I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know if he was related to General Vlastimir Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be certain, but if Goran Djordjevic -- well, I know that he was a police officer in the Podujevo police station at the time when I was the commander, and I know that he hails from Nis, and he never mentioned anything. So if it is the same man, I do know him quite well, and he never mentioned that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know if he is or not. I was just asking if you knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender 1591 at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00763, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, next I'd like to direct your attention to Exhibit P133. This is tab 15 in your binder. I don't know if this one of the documents that Mr. Stamp showed you or not. Have you seen this particular before? It's dated the 28th July, 1998, and it appears to be a MUP dispatch assigning or deploying certain PJP detachments to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document a couple of days ago. Mr. Stamp showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you see this document in 1998, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you see documents like this in 1998 or 1999? And I'm referring to dispatches from the ministry sending or deploying PJP units to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must have seen a dispatch of this kind, but they did not pertain to me. So I cannot rule out the possibility that I saw it, but I can't remember specifically because it was not addressed to me, attention to me. I may have seen it in passing on somebody else's desk, but I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This one makes reference to certain detachments to be deployed, and you'll see that the 66th Detachment was to be deployed to Pristina. Do you recall in July 1998 whether the 66th Detachment of the PJP arrived in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You don't think it arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Did you ever have any dealings with that particular PJP detachment?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me show you next tab number 17. This is Exhibit P356. This is a dispatch dated the 18th of February, 1999, from General Djordjevic. Going to, among others, all the SUP chiefs, to the ministry staff in Pristina, to the border police stations. I see it's not addressed to you, but I have a couple questions that you may be able to help us with. Item number 1 calls upon the addressees to update the defence plan, and in particular update establishment lists of active and reserve policemen, recruit to full capacity the 21st to the 87th Detachments in the PJPs, carry out a troop review, et cetera. Can you recall now what the defence plan was that was in place for the MUP in February of 1999, in general?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really be certain, but I assume that it was a plan for the defence of the facilities or installations of the MUP, the key, vital facilities. I assume that that is what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know whether this action was carried out, that is, updating and recruiting to full capacity for the 21st through the 87th PJP Detachments?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume yes. But when the lists were updated the staff -- for the staffing level from the 21st and to the 88th PJP Detachments, I can say only for the two companies and the 124th Intervention Brigade because as the department chief they were under my aegis as regards the staffing levels. I was in charge of that, so I can only speak about those.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what can you say about those of yours?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the two companies you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that if the companies were not at full strength, then new personnel would be brought in; they would be reinforced. And that's probably what was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if that was done in February 1999, about a month before the NATO bombing began?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't recall if it was done, but in light of the dispatch and the orders contained therein, I assumed that it was the case. But I can't now remember with complete certainty whether it was done and how it was done, in what way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Could you turn to item number 7 in that dispatch. And my English translation has that as directing: "Through intensified intelligence and other measures and actions, carry out the necessary checks, compile lists, and establish complete control over volunteer and paramilitary units and their members." In February 1999 were you aware of the existence in Kosovo of paramilitary units or volunteer units?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At any time in 1998 or 1999, were you personally aware of the existence of such units?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know why General Djordjevic would be directing that that kind of activity be carried out, unless there were such units in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to intervene because I believe that this is a leading question because you can see from the title that this dispatch was sent to all Secretariats of the Interior from 1 through 33, not only in Kosovo and Metohija, so it's a tendentious question. This pertains to the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, if I rephrase my question, do you know why General Djordjevic would be directing that kind of activity be carried out unless there was such units in Serbia in 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you what the reasons were behind this dispatch. What I know about the territory covered by the secretariat where I worked, there were no paramilitary or volunteer units. Maybe there was some knowledge or perhaps some concern that in some areas of the republic there might be or would be such units, I can't really tell you, or indeed that there were some units somewhere, I can't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you next item 22 -- tab 22 in the binder. This is 65 ter number 01989. And these are described as the minutes of a meeting with senior police officials in Kosovo and Metohija, 4th of April, 1999. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during my proofing for my testimony here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I know that under the agenda, the three agenda items, it says that the meeting was held by General Stevanovic and General Lukic, and it was attended by the chiefs of all secretariats, PJP detachment commanders, the SAJ commander, and the JSO commander, among others. As brigade commander of the 124th, did you attend this meeting? I don't see you listed as speaking, but the it says "detachment commanders." Do you recall if you were there or not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really tell you with complete certainty, but in all likelihood, yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And among those speaking were the SAJ commander Zivko Trajkovic. I think you told us yesterday that you knew him. When would you see Commander Trajkovic in Kosovo? Would it be at meetings like this, or did you have any other dealings with him in your position as brigade commander for the PJP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would usually see him at meetings, but sometimes it would happen, admittedly not often, that we would run into each other in the field. Now I'm primarily talking about 1998 not 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the JSO commander is listed, he's the second speaker after Trajkovic. And the name mentioned is Milorad Jankovic. Did you know a Milorad Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know Milorad Jankovic. I assume there is an error here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's what I was curious about, because I know yesterday we looked at Exhibit P57, which was the 16 June 1998 decision by the minister establishing a staff for the suppression of terrorism, and it listed the JSO commander as being Milorad Lukovic. Is that the person you knew to be the JSO commander in April of 1999 in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So I think that's probably a typographical error.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And your -- what dealings, if any, did you have with a Milorad Lukovic in Kosovo in 1998 or 1999, other than seeing him at a meeting like this? Did you have any other occasion to work with him?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And his nickname was Legija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to ask you about --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could I tender that before I move on, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00764, Your Honours, that's for document ID 65 ter 01989.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, if you could turn next to tab 23 in your binder. Now, this is -- this is a VJ document and the number --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The 65 ter number of this one, Your Honours, is 02821.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's dated the 19th of May, 1999, from Colonel Bozidar Delic at the -- who was the commander of the 549th Motorised Brigade. Did you see this document when you were being prepared to testify by Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that the first time you ever saw it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about item number 3. I think it's on page 1 of your document. It says: "The 5/124th OdPJP in coordinated action with other defence forces shall carry out combat control of the territory ..." And then it describes the location. Can you tell me what that stands for. Is that the 5th Company of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the 5th Company of the 124th Detachment, and I'm quoting as it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's not a brigade but a PJP detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was there 124th PJP Detachment that was something distinct, separate, from your 124th Intervention Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Such a thing did not exist. I suppose that what it's meant here is the 5th Company of the 124th Intervention Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, this is probably a typo or an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Or it could be that Colonel Delic wasn't all that familiar with the MUP designations, and since most of the others were detachments, he assumed the 124th was a detachment as well?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did any of the other detachments have as many as five companies within them?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that every detachment had five or more companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know if in May -- on or about May 19th, 1999, the 5th Company of your brigade was involved in a coordinated action with the VJ in the area of Pirane, Landovica, and Novaki villages in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of your 5th company was at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. It was Lieutenant-Colonel Veljko Radenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you look at number 9 in this order, the last item. It says: "Detachments commands of the PJP shall issue orders regulating all other issues within their domain related to the units life and operations. That will be done according to positive rules in force in our previous orders." I know in your statement you've talked a little bit about how these joint operations with the VJ worked. Is what's written here consistent with your experience in real life in these joint operations about how a command worked within the MUP when you were working jointly in combat operations with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to repeat your question because I'm not entirely sure that I understood your question properly the first time around.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, maybe I should rephrase it because I'm not trying to put words in your mouth. But could you describe --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be good.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you describe for us how the coordination worked with the VJ when these joint combat actions or operations were carried out. Who was in command of the MUP units for which purposes, if you will? Can you elaborate on that for us?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Interpretation] As you can see in the document, the order was signed by commander Colonel Delic. I assume that -- just a moment. Could you please bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me very concretely about this particular order, this order applies more to the deployment of units which were in charge of the combat control of the territory. This means that they were supposed to be in a certain territory, and they were supposed not to allow terrorist groups or anybody else to appear that might have posed a threat to security. And you can see that some tasks were issued, which wings, which flanks, which units, which roads to be very precise in terms of this document, as far as this document is concerned. I don't think that this is an order for the execution of a concrete task or action. This is an order regarding the control of a territory following an action or an operation or a territory that has to be placed under control, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I take your point. We'll look at -- in a minute or two at some more specific combat-related action orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender that now before I go to the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 02821, Your Honours, will be assigned P00765.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, if you turn next to tab 47 in your binder, and this is 65 ter number 04057. It's dated the 9th of April, 1999, from General Lazarevic of the Pristina Corps command. I don't know, did Mr. Stamp show you this document when he proofed you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You see the -- and it is an internal VJ document, but -- and you may be able to help us with some of this. The second paragraph says: "The staff of the Serbian MUP for Kosovo and Metohija has issued an order to all secretariats to commence planning actions to crush the terrorist groups that remained in the respective zones of responsibility." Do you recall that having been done, that the secretariats had an order to plan actions, anti-terrorist actions, within their own zones on or about the 9th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any such order having been issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not anti-terrorist actions were planned within your Pristina SUP in April 1999? Do you recollect any?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you'll continue down on that document General Lazarevic is directing his subordinates to: " ... coordinate actions with MUP units in crushing the Siptar terrorist forces, immediately establish contact with SUP chiefs concerning the following ..." And then item number 1 is for the Pristina SUP, and it lists three different actions, the first being in the Kosmac Donje Obrinje area, second in Kacanik area, and the third in Orlane apparently and specifying the VJ units that were going to participate. Do any of those look familiar to you as actions that the Pristina SUP or your brigade assisted or cooperated with the VJ on in April of 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any of that as having happened and having involved MUP forces. I'm not excluding others, but those that I worked with, I don't think so. And I believe that here under 1 or 2, Kacanik action, this is not part of the territory of the Pristina secretariat but rather of the Urosevac secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did any members of your 124th Intervention Brigade participate in joint combat actions with any of these VJ units, the 15th Armoured Brigade, the 37th Motorised Brigade, the 354th Infantry Brigade, or the 211th Armoured Brigade in April of 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just said that I don't think so, at least not to my knowledge. Maybe some other units were engaged in that way, but I was not involved. I was not part of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Let me move then to tab 57, and tab 57 is 65 ter number 01971. This is a Joint Command order dated the 13th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Everybody is concerned you haven't sought to tender this, Mr. Hannis, and I suspect I know that you've decided not to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't feel comfortable in doing that. Given his answers about the document and given that it's a VJ document, I think it's more appropriate to do it later with someone else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I appreciate the concern of my colleagues to keep me on track.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is dated the 13th of April, 1999, and it's for -- it's an order on routing and destroying Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Zegovac. I understood from the notes I got from Mr. Stamp that he talked or showed this -- showed this one to you, and this was a joint action that you were familiar with. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And the VJ units involved in this action were the 252nd Tactical Group which included our battalion and the 175th Intervention Brigade. Do you recall which units assisted in this action?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can recall properly, I believe that parts of several companies from the 124th Intervention Brigade participated, also some of the units of the 36th Detachment, and I believe that SAJ as well was involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, this particular order itself, did you see orders like this in 1998 or 1999 coming from a body called the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see similar orders similar to this one, but I must be honest and admit that at that time I believe that all orders had been issued by the corps command, the corps command of the military. Judging by the content and everything else, that's what they looked like. I did not pay too much attention to the heading of these orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I agree with you. The number and the format all seem to be consistent with Pristina Corps documents at the time, and I think that's what General Lazarevic would say as well. So I'm not trying to mislead you or trick you on anything here, but that is what it says on the document. But how would you see these orders? How did you come to see a copy? Did someone deliver it to you, or did you pick it up from someone? How would you see them?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody would submit them, or I would go to a meeting where it was agreed to carry out preparations for an action including reconnoitring of the area of the future action, and I would receive a document similar to this one. It would be an order for the execution of a task. And I would also be given a map which we called a decision for the execution of task, and we would receive the topical excerpt and concerned the task of my units as it were. Whatever is contained in the order would be also transferred on to the map. So when you receive an order, when you receive a map, and having been familiarised with certain items of the order, it happened very rarely that you look at the order with a lot of attention because you look at the decision, a map with the deployment of all units depicted there, you look at the ground and all the neighbouring units. If you only read the order, you can't gain a similar impression, such a detailed impression. For us the main document was that decision on the map, and this was what governed us in the execution of the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, that makes sense to me that the map showing the positions of the units and the enemy and the directions of movement, et cetera, would be more important to you in carrying out a task like that; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less that would be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as brigade commander did you actually go out in the field on some of these joint VJ/MUP anti-terrorist actions in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is implied.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to be sure it was the correct interpretation of what you did, and I think in your statement you indicated that -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Let me just add that applied to actions where I as a unit commander participated with parts of my unit and not to all the preparations for the action that involved some other parts, some other companies, which cooperated with other units. In that latter case I wouldn't go, but when I was engaged as a unit commander with parts of my unit, that was implied.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. Thank you. And when you got copies of these orders and the decision maps as I would refer to them, who did you actually physically get that from? Was that somebody in the MUP or somebody in the VJ or did it -- did it change from time to time who you got it from?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, when that happened in the field I believe that we received this from our colleagues -- from our colleagues in the military. And when this happened in some rooms, on some premises, then this would be delivered to us at times in envelopes, or it would be handed over to us in envelopes. I believe that this was done by people from the MUP staff. I'm sure that the envelopes were delivered to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know who in the MUP staff was primarily responsible for coordination or liaising with the VJ for purposes of joint VJ/MUP combat activities? Was there a particular person?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably existed, but I don't know who it was. This was command superior to me, a higher command, so I can't say with any degree of certainty who that person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know if, first name, Dusko Adamovic ever performed that function?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume, knowing that he was a member of the staff, but I can't say with certainty that he was the one who did it because I did not have an occasion to see him in action, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever receive any of these orders or decision maps from him?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- I suppose so, most probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about in the VJ, did you ever -- no, apart from in the field, where you might have met face-to-face with a VJ field commander, but did you have any dealings concerning these decision maps or the orders for joint actions? Did you receive any from anybody in the VJ, from the Pristina Corps, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I just said that if we received that in the field directly during meetings concerning the execution of a concrete task of reconnoitring, then the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever meet or deal with a VJ officer named Radojko Stefanovic in connection with these kind of coordinating activities?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to coordinating activities, if I'm not mistaken, the answer's no. And as for Radojko Stefanovic, I was with him, if I'm not mistaken, in the last action before the signing of the Kumanovo Agreement. I can't remember the exact title of the action now, but I know that it was in the territory of a place called Berisa. He was present there on behalf of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that one now, if I may, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 01971, Your Honours, will be assigned P00766.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if you could go to the next tab in your binder, it's tab 58, General. This is a similar Joint Command order dated the 15th of April, 1999, and it's an order for the routing and destroying of the Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Jezerce. Were you shown this document when you were being proofed? And I should indicate this is 65 ter number 01976 -- I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think this is an action that you were familiar with; right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did participate directly in this action.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And which of your subordinate PJP companies took part, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is evident that this action was a somewhat broader action, and it comprised a number of units of the military and a number of police units as well. I was directly engaged in one part of the terrain together with, if I'm not mistaken, four PJP companies. From the strength of my unit I coordinated their work, and I was in charge of their work on the Urosevac - Gornje and Donje Nerodimlje - and Stojkovici axis. I believe those were the names of the villages. Our task within the overall mission was to take some of the evelations [as interpreted] which are known as the Jezersko mountain range. We accomplished the task in the course of the first day. There was one part of the task which we could not objectively carry out because of the other participating units. Once the conditions were in place, we managed to accomplish those tasks as well. Generally speaking, it was one of the easier tasks that I participated in, in terms of the speed. However, the whole thing lasted quite a long time, and the conditions were very difficult for the men who participated in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall which specific VJ units you worked with on that occasion? Those listed in the order included the 252nd Tactical Group, the 243rd Mechanised Brigade and the 549th. Do you recall which ones you might have worked most closely with?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the 252nd, that's the Tactical Group 252.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because even in the task TG 525, it says set up a blockade on the line Stimlje-Kosare-Gornje Nerodimlje; that's what I said. That's the axis that we had as our designated axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I would like to tender that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be assigned P00767, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And related to that I'd next like to show you tab 21. This document is 65 ter number 03081. This is a war diary of the 549th Motorised Brigade. And I just want to ask you about an entry in there if you can help clarify something for me. I think it's page 53 of the B/C/S under tab 21. It's a very thick document. Do you find that? It's the fattest document in your binder, I believe. And we're looking at page 33 in the English. I'll tell you this is part of an entry for the 26th of April, 1999. And I don't know if you can find -- in the upper right-hand corner there may be a page number 53 written. Do you see any numbers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is page 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it's in e-court as well. It may be on the screen. I think that tab there indicates the page actually. And you see there's a reference to --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've been able to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The entry says: "In the course of the day, MUP units supported by parts of the brigade's units continued destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in Budakovo and the village of Jezerce. During the course of the day the total number of units grew by two detachments of MUP special police and of Pristina SAJ ..." What was the Pristina SAJ? Did the Pristina SUP have a SAJ unit within it or was the -- can you tell us what that refers to, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special anti-terrorist unit, the name itself tells you that this is a unit for special anti-terrorist tasks, so it was not part of the Pristina SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Was it based in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was based in a place near Pristina, Ajvalija.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, I've heard that. Thank you. And the MUP special police, the PJP, would have been assisting the 549th Brigade in this area. Do you know which company or which detachments those were?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As indicated in this document, it says the Budakovo-Jezerce village axis. So that is the axis that goes in the opposite direction from the axis where I was, so that I really don't know what units took part, MUP or military units. But one can conclude that it was part of the 400 -- 549th Brigade of the military of the Yugoslav Army because that was their area, but I really don't know. I assume that the distance as the crow flies was maybe some 20 kilometres or more because Budakovo -- well, I never went there, but Budakovo is further down from Suva Reka, and if you go towards the Jezersko mountains. I was never in that area so I can't really tell you. That's just my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to turn to your statement. In paragraph 16 you make reference to having heard about the existence of the Joint Command, and you said you'd thought you'd heard of it by the second half of 1998. You --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I don't want to tender that diary at this point in time, Your Honours. I think it's premature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You said that you also became more aware generally of the existence of the Joint Command after the war when you came across a reference to it in a book on compliance with the Laws of War published by the VJ. I want to show you a document, and I ask you if this is the book you're referring to. This would be document 65 ter number 01011. You don't have a hard copy in your binder so you'll have to look on the screen with me. I see the English version. I don't know if you see a B/C/S version on your screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Well, in advance, since we are now about to address a new topic in this trial, what is the status of some books that were read after the relevant period and the evidence of the witness regarding something he read afterwards? Just so I could be guided by the precedence, so that I could deal with the same issues in the course of my Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is no short or general answer to your question, Mr. Djurdjic. Among other things, we would look at the nature of the authorship, the responsibility of any office held by the author, whether it was an article purporting to reflect the activity, for example, of the Yugoslav Army at a particular time written by a member of that army or whether it was some other study. All of those things would determine for the Chamber what relevance and assistance a book written after the event might be. We start with the question that you are posing. This is something after the event; therefore, how is it relevant? Unless there's a clear answer to that, a positive answer, then it would not be admitted. But we will look more at this work as it is unfolded and see what we make of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm just trying to establish, is this the book that you were referring to your statement? Can you tell by looking at the cover?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think so. I was not in a position to take this book into my hands and read it to the end. I remember seeing it somewhere, but I don't know where. And as I leafed through it I saw what I've just told you. It is not a book that I had in my possession; it is not at a book that I read or studied. It's simply a book that I happened upon, and I leafed through it and saw those elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you a specific page and see if that will help. I think it's page 51 of the B/C/S in e-court, and page in English is page 72. I'm going to show you a page in this book that makes a reference to Joint Command, and maybe when you see it in your B/C/S version -- on the right you'll see -- in the right column you'll see a document that looks like a cover page of a document, and there are a couple of circled portions of excerpts from that document. And I think the title of that is Joint Command for KM, Kosovo and Metohija, and it's a report and conclusions on the implementation of the plan for stamping out terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. Does that help you remember whether or not this may have been the book that was the source of your post-war additional information about the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't confirm on the basis of the front page, but on the basis of the details from the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You'll see -- we may have to show you the entire B/C/S page, but the English translation, paragraph related to this cover page says: "In the report and conclusions on the implementation of the plan on stamping out terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija of November [sic] 1998 signed by the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija, the course and consequences of operations by the Yugoslav Army and MUP units between 25 and 29 September 1998 are analysed in detail." And it goes on. Does that ring any bells? I'm just trying to find out if this is the document you're talking about in your statement, or if there's another one I should be trying to find. If you remember or you don't remember, just let me know and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the details, the specific details, from the book, but this is the book where I saw it. Now, as to what details are actually -- I actually saw, a long time has passed, and I never have seen them again. But I think that more or less this is the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I don't have any other questions about that then. I want to go back to your statement. In paragraph 19 of your statement you mention that after combat operations PJP personnel were required to account for spent ammunition. How was that done? Did each soldier count the number of bullets he had used and then report that to a commander, who gave you a report? How was that reported? Orally? Written?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the war started the consumption of ammunition was justified unit by unit because to get re-supplied with ammunition that you needed for your next mission, you had to write a report indicating that in such and such action you expended a certain quantity of ammunition and that, therefore, you needed additional quantities of ammunition. And this is what you quoted back to me from my statement refers to. So it would be only logical for it to be determined from the level of the individual up to the level of the unit. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And that written report concerning the use of ammunition, did it have any other report about the action in which the ammunition was used? Or did it only report on quantities used with no further detail about where, how, why?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't remember those details.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did -- during 1998 and 1999 as brigade commander, did you ever prepare written reports concerning combat actions or anti-terrorist actions carried out by your subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my duty to draft in the second half of 1999 a report, but we didn't do reports for every single action. It was, I assume, done by the military unit that took part in the same task together with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You said it was your duty to draft in the second half of 1999 a report. What kind of report? Was that a report about all the actions of your unit prior to that date or during the war? What was that report? A summary of all those actions?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's a comprehensive report for 1998 and 1999, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And to whom was that report sent?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was sent to the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In MUP headquarters at the republic level?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the police administration within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who was the head of that administration at that time, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me right, I don't think that there was a chief in that administration at that time. That's what I think. There was only the deputy chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And was the assistant minister in charge of that administration Obrad Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether that was his duty, but Ljuba Aleksic was the deputy chief of the administration, so I assume that he performed the duties of the administration chief because when the administration chief is not there, then it's the deputy chief who acts in his stead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I don't think I've ever seen that report. Do you have a copy?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were there any other copies sent by you to anyone else other than to the police administration in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to the police administration and the ministry; that was the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who did the order come from?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you with complete certainty who it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You don't know the name or the title or the organ from which the order came to write this report?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I simply can't remember what organ actually sent it. It may have been the police administration, for instance, but as I said I can't remember so I'm not sure if that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately when you received the order to do that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I'm not mistaken it was sometime in the second half of 1999. I can't give you the month because I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, how long a report was this? You're talking about a one- or two-page report, or was it 40 or 50 pages? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My report?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it had several pages. I don't know how many pages but several because it contained quite a lot of other details. It was not just a report about the specific missions. It had to do with equipment, weapons. So quite a lot of things were covered in it, and those things took up more space in the report than the actual reports about the missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you'll understand my interest in this report because it was written by you shortly after the events when things were fresh in your mind, and you, yourself, have indicated how difficult it is sometimes to remember now, ten years later. What odd document -- what documents did you use to create your report at that time? Or did you just write it based on what was in your head?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the report as such was not drafted by myself. It was actually drafted by my associates. It was their duty to do that, and they were drafted on the basis of the reports from the company commanders that we received from them, so we simply put all this together.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it these are written reports from company commanders; right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know where those written reports from PJP company commanders would be today?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, at the time when this report was drafted, I was headquartered in the Secretariat of the Interior in Pristina, and the headquarters was relocated to Niska Banja in a building that had just a couple of rooms, and that's where the report was drafted. And since this report is classified as confidential or strictly confidential, I had to produce just one copy and then submit it. And the reports from the company commanders that I received, since I didn't have the wherewithal to keep them in the manner that was prescribed, I was forced to return them to the company commanders for their safe keeping because I didn't want to have any problems because that might have led to the disclosure of state secrets, and that would have engendered a number of problems. And that's why I produced just one copy and returned back the originals to them, thinking that I would be able to consult them if necessary later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you give us the names of your colleagues who helped you prepare this report?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can, but I don't want to leave anyone out. I think that Dragan Simic took part, and I think Nebojsa Sindic, I think that some other people also helped out, the late Dimitrijevic. I really can't give you all of the names, but those people for the most part drafted the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you haven't seen that document since you prepared it and sent it on in 1999; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us about how when you prepared for coming here to testify that you requested some documents, and that's when you got to see, I think for the first time, Exhibit P57, the decision by Minister Stojiljkovic creating the MUP staff for suppression of terrorism. At that time did you request to see your report, because that seems like that would have been one of the most useful things for you to have to prepare for your testimony here? Did you ask to get a copy of it then?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the archive that I stated was at my disposal, all the documents are listed there. So what I was interested in was to find this report, but among the documents I didn't see this report as existing -- listed as existing in the archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when you didn't see it on the list, did you ask if someone could search for it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't asking around because a while ago, maybe two years ago, something like that, I was asked the same question that you're now asking me about this report, and I gave the same answer. And I realised from discussing it with my colleague that there is a problem because those reports are missing. That is the impression I got. I don't know whether it's just my report, but I, at any rate, was made aware of the fact that there was a problem there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall who made you aware of the problem, the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean who came to me with this request?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, who was the person that made you aware that some of these reports were missing and that there was a problem there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly. I think that it is Goran Markovic, I think that's his name, in the ministry. He is part of the service for the detection of crimes, one of the departments dealing with the Tribunal, if my memory serves me right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know I'm at the limit of what I said I thought I was going to take today, but it's taking me longer. I think this witness is a very important witness for us. I -- the only thing I think I have left to do with him is I want to talk about some MUP staff meetings in 1999. There are about six or seven of those meetings, and then I would be done, but I would ask leave to do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Continue after the break --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- Mr. Hannis. We will have the first break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sir, before I go to some meetings of the MUP staff in 1998 and 1999, I wanted to ask you about your current position. What is your current position, you're still with the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's your title and generally your duties?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am an advisor in the police direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rather, administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what kind of duties do you have as advisor?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I'm given to do, whatever tasks I'm given to do. I don't have any strict orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let me show you first tab 27. This is 65 ter number 04151. I believe Mr. Stamp may have shown you most of these MUP meetings. This one is dated the 22nd of July, 1998, and among the attendees listed along with General Djordjevic, Stevanovic, and Lukic, it mentions all commanders of PJP detachments. Do you recall having seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not before. Not before I was shown the document by your colleague, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall if you attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure; however, if my name's there then I suppose I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You see under the agenda items, item number 3 says: "Defining task in the implementation of the global plan and the following task ..." Do you remember what the global plan was, what that referred to in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday at the very outset I said that I did not have my own notes. They had been destroyed, so I did not have any -- anything to jog my memory as to that meeting were my possible notes that would provide any suggestions. From what I could read in the minutes, I really can't remember what the meeting was all about. It says here that chiefs of the SUP provide their briefings and nothing else which doesn't help me to remember what the meeting was all about. If I saw any of the documents elaborating on items two or three, maybe that would help.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this: Did you ever hear the term used in 1998, the term "plan for combatting terrorism in Kosovo" or "plan for suppressing terrorism or fighting terrorism in Kosovo"? Did you hear of that plan?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of particular individual actions. I really didn't know that there was a general plan. I suppose that this is down to my level, the strength of my forces, all that restricted my access to information, I would say. There may have been such a plan, but I wouldn't know, I didn't know of any such plan. From where I stood, there were concrete plans for concrete tasks and missions, and that's what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you didn't hear the term -- here it's in capital letters "global plan" discussed either in this meeting or among other MUP colleagues in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you hear any complaints among the senior staff of the MUP about the VJ or General Pavkovic coming up with this overall plan for fighting terrorism that was going to require a lot of extra work by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At my level I did not hear that. As for the levels above me, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to tender that if I may, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00768, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you could go to the next tab, General, tab 28, this is at 65 ter number 04152. This is dated the 26th of October, 1998. Attendees include commanders of the PJP. Did you see this document with Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you might have attended this particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that I attended this particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And General Stevanovic is informing the group about the agreement with the OSCE, and could you look at item number 13, that's the last one. It says: "Reinforce Serb villages with reservists as required ... " Do you know if that was done at this time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. If it's written in there, then I suppose it's correct; however, I can't give you any more detail because I simply can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember that part of the agreement, the Milosevic-Holbrooke Agreement in late October 1998 called for a reduction of the number of policemen in Kosovo, I think something on the level of 4.000 men or so were supposed to be taken out of Kosovo and returned to Serbia proper. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this meeting very well for two reasons, the first one being the fact that we waited several hours for the meeting to begin because General [indiscernible] came directly from Belgrade after the signing of the agreement. I can't remember the details, but I believe that it was about the reduction of the MUP strength, and I also know that the police was given a task to - if I'm not mistaken - the routes that had been defined by the agreements, that the police could stay there as well as in some observation posts. I believe that the number of the observation posts was also defined. It was a long time ago so I can't remember the details very clearly, but the meeting was important because it was about the implementation, and that is very clear still in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You'll see on the first page item number 1 it says that: "A plan needs to be made and the number of engaged units reduced by 4.500 members of the police force." Do you remember that being discussed at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was discussed, but I would not be able to give you any concrete numbers. I believe that what is written here, I will allow the possibility that that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm trying to figure out how item 13 about reinforcing the Serb villages with reservists ties in to that reduction of force by 4.5 00. Was that a way to try to make up for the reduction in the regular force, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the same number of men, within the same strength, you can move people in order to focus on a certain task, and I'm saying this in more general terms, not in any ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we tender that one, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00769, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next one is tab 29. This is Exhibit P690 already in evidence. This is a meeting on the 3rd of November, 1998 -- well, actually it's conclusions about the meeting. Did you ever see this document?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. It says -- this is conclusions from a meeting on -- that was held on the 2nd of November, 1998, with secretariat chiefs and police detachment commanders. Do you recall if you attended such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say with any degree of certainty; however, if you can read it in the document, then, yes, as I did indeed attend most of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I want to ask you about some of the conclusions from that meeting, see if you recall those events. Item number 6 -- and this is in connection with the OSCE agreement. "Armoured vehicles and weapons of a calibre larger than 7.9 millimetre must not be used, engaged, or moved without agreement and permission from the Staff." Do you recall, was that placed in effect at that time? Did you have to get permission to use those larger-calibre weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to remember, but if we can read it in the document, then I believe that that was the case and that it was observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Look at item number 8. I think this relates to the last one we looked at where it talked about reinforcing the Serb villages with reserves. I'll read part of it to you. "In villages with Serbian inhabitants, take additional protection measures ..." And the next sentence goes on to say: "Make sure that Serbs and members of the RPO," which is translated as reserve police squads, "do not misuse weapons, let off guns at weddings," et cetera, "do not carry weapons or show them in public the presence of members of the mission. When on guard duty, use one weapon and prevent individuals from bringing in the weapon they have been issued. Tell them not to state the fact that Serbs are armed and to explain this fact, if they must, using the excuse that it is only members of the guard who are armed." First of all, do you remember that being discussed or concluded at this meeting in November 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were aware, though, that the Serbs in Kosovo had been issued weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that arms were distributed to the population -- to the population in the villages with mixed populations. That was to help them protect themselves from terrorists who were numerous at the time, and that was the main objective of the exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But wasn't it only that the Serbs who were issued the weapons, not Albanians, not Kosovo Albanians?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs were issued weapons in the villages with mixed populations or predominantly inhabited by the Serbs, and I told you what the reason for that was, in order to help them protect themselves from terrorist attacks. At the time there were a lot of terrorists around. I suppose that there were no terrorist attacks against Albanians, which makes me conclude that weapons were not issued to them also. But as far as I know, some Albanians were also issued weapons if they were under terrorist threats whose houses had come under attack. And also the Roma population was issued weapons. So that would be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What Albanians do you know of that were issued weapons by the Serb authorities? Can you tell me a village or any particular individuals in 1998 or 1999 that got issued weapons by the Serb VJ or the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really wouldn't be able to give you any names, but I know that there were such cases. This was not my main area of concern, so I wouldn't be able to give you any individual names. But from experience and from what my colleagues told me and from what I heard on TV, I know there were villages where people of Albanian ethnicity were given weapons for their personal protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's move to item number 10. It says: "The MUP staff in Pristina will now take on the role of planning, and the Secretariats will have greater independence in carrying out their regular duties ..." And then the last sentence says: "Commanders and deputy-commanders will take command of the dispatched units - 'A' units of the PJP - and all units come under the Secretariats." First of all, can you tell me what's the difference between an A unit and a B unit of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were the so-called A formation detachments that we have already mentioned, and there were also the so-called B formation detachments. I don't know their numerical designations, but I believe that those were the 72nd, 73rd, 85th, 86th, 87th. If I'm not mistaken, the difference lay in the fact that the A formation detachments were composed of better-trained police members.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I've heard one explanation that the A units were considered the manoeuvre units, the ones who actually went out in the field and did combat; and B units were reserve units who kind of stuck closer to home and did duties like, I don't know, setting a blockade or setting a perimeter, et cetera. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me move on, then, to tab 30. This is 65 ter number 02805, dated the 5th of November, 1998. A meeting that was attended by President Milutinovic and the Minister of the Interior Stojiljkovic, General Djordjevic, and others, as well as the commanders of the PJP. The meeting was chaired by General Lukic, according to the minutes, which were taken by Desimir Slovic. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see it with Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall being present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I should recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it would be unusual for the president to be there, so it seems like that would be a meeting you would remember if you were at. I see you shaking your head yes, you agree. You'll have to answer out loud.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, but when it comes to the meetings in 1998, at that time I had some personal problems. My mother was seriously and lethally ill, so I had a lot of commitments with this regard. I was in Pristina. She was in hospital in Belgrade. I had to travel a lot for that reason, so that's why I'm saying that there is a possibility that I did not attend some of the meetings which was always justified with the knowledge of my superiors who -- excuse me, that's why I'm saying with a reservation there's no doubt about the fact that I attended a lot of the meetings. I probably attended this one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You don't have any reason to doubt that this is an accurate or authentic document?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mean you absolutely don't have a doubt?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The one thing I had wanted to ask you about was something that President Milutinovic is recorded as having said. You'll see where he's speaking and, I don't know, it's -- I'm not sure where it is on your page. I think it may be marked in orange to help guide you to it. And he's saying -- he's talking about a meeting that was held I think just a few days before, on the 29th of October, 1998, and he says: "With regard to the Yugoslav army and police everything will stay the same as it has been up to now, a Joint Command, VJ units will not withdraw, and police forces have only been reduced by the number that has already been withdrawn." Does that refresh your memory about whether or not you may have been at this meeting, because there's a reference to the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on only that detail, I don't think so, but I know that there was a meeting which was attended by President Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender that exhibit at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00770, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, next I would like to show you tab 31. This is exhibit in evidence P689, dated 2 December 1998, minutes of a meeting of MUP staff, SUP chiefs, and commanders of PJP units. Did Mr. Stamp show you this one?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, actually. Maybe yes, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I know that page 5 in my English and I think on page 5 of your copy, there's a note that the commanders of the detachments did not speak, so there's no indication that you or any other PJP commander spoke at the meeting. But I want to ask you about something on the last page. Coming up from the bottom you'll see a list of items number 1 through 8, and above that there are some bullet points. It's the fifth one up. It says: "Commanders of detachments are members of the collegium of the chief of the SUP and should be linked up daily with the chief of the SUP for purposes of work and control." Do you know, did that happen in your SUP? Were you linked up daily with the chief of the SUP as a detachment or a brigade commander of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not liaising with the chief of the SUP in that capacity, but in the capacity as the chief of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In your capacity as brigade commander, who would you liaise with if not the chief of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yesterday I think that I was linked up at the time when the brigade would receive specific tasks to carry out some kind of an anti-terrorist action. Here we're talking about regular duties, regular work, and the brigade was not involved in it in a number that would require my participation. So I was not part of that communication, but as the chief of the police department, definitely I was, of the OUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's move to the next one, tab 32 in your binder, this is exhibit in evidence P85, 085. This one, General, is dated the 17th of February, 1999, Pristina MUP staff meeting. This one was attended by the Minister of the Interior, General Djordjevic, General Stevanovic, some others. It says the PJP commanders are present. Did Mr. Stamp show you this one?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you were present for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. General Lukic is the first speaker, and one of the things he's talking about is reserve police stations. At the bottom of your page 1, two or three lines up from the bottom it says: "A plan of the RJB, public security department, has been worked out to prevent and thwart the entry of NATO troops into our territory. The staff plans, when it is ordered, to carry out three mopping up operations in the Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica areas and has allotted around 4.000 policemen" some OPG policemen and some reserves. Do you recall that being discussed at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall the details of the meeting, but if that's what it says here, there's no reason for me to doubt that this was actually how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And it continues on to the next page, and it says: "On Saturday 20 February 1999 a meeting of the staff will be held with all police unit detachment commanders for further consultations about their engagement." Was that meeting held and did you attend?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really say with any certainty whether I was present there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And again it mentions meetings being held with the reserve police stations. Under whose command were the reserve police stations? Do you know what the structure was there of the hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reserve police sections were set up -- well, we have already explained that they had their commanders and the commanders were in contact with one of the commanding officers in the police stations, informing them about all of the incidents, any changes, and any needs that arose for any assistance, if there was an attack, things of that nature. But the task of those reserve police departments or sections was exclusively to defend the inhabited area against any kind of defence or any threat, and also to protect some infrastructural facilities, transformer stations, water-supply systems, whatever was key or vital in those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was it a regular policeman or police officer, then, who would be in charge to those reserve police contingents?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think when you say "regular," the commanders of those reserve police departments, that they were probably reserve police officers from those locations. And it was their duty to be in touch with some of the commanding officers in the police station that covered that area in order to coordinate all those things that had to be coordinated in order for them to get any assistance when it was needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Well, let me take you to the next one. This is tab 33 in your binder, General, 65 ter number 01996, minutes of a MUP staff meeting on 7 May 1999 in Pristina attended by Deputy Prime Minister Mr. Sainovic, General Obrad Stevanovic, some of the MUP staff, chiefs of SUP.
