I can't tell if PJP officers attended or not; they're not listed. Did Mr. Stamp show you this document?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you attended such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me take you to -- I think it's the next-to-the-last page, page 9 in the B/C/S or in the Serbian version, it's page 11 in the English. You might be able to help us with some of the things that were mentioned there. This is General Stevanovic talking, and item number 2 says: "Anti-terrorist actions ..." do you find that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He says: "After the end of some of the larger actions such as Budakovo-Jezerce, each SUP will be expected to work independently on organising anti-terrorist actions in their own areas. The plan must be approved by the staff and will be carried out together with manoeuvre detachments ..." Do you recall after that big operation in Budakovo-Jezerce, was this done? Did each SUP make their own plans for anti-terrorist actions in their area or in your area, in Pristina SUP area?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, and I don't think that any independent actions were actually carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know if any were planned but not carried out?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with me, and I don't think that that was the case in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me take you to item number 4: "Defence from ground attacks ..." The second bullet point says: "It is very likely that, apart from the 124th," here it says, "Special Police Detachment, our PJP manoeuvre detachments will participate in the defence against any ground attacks ..." First of all, it says "OPJP." Is that special police detachment like we saw before but it probably should be brigade? Because I think you told me there was no 124th PJP Detachment.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it is. But what I'm reading here is not clear to me. I couldn't really --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to hear that. I was hoping you could help me because it's not clear to me either. I'm trying to figure out why would the 124th not be involved in participating in the defence against ground attacks? Was the 124th Brigade being reserved for some other tasks, some more important tasks, some special or different task? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is really the first time that I see it. Please take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And after this date of the 7th of May, 1999, was anything different being done with regard to how your intervention brigade was being used?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, under the same conditions as were valid before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you will go then farther down two paragraphs, my English says: "In the organisation of work, the Secretariat of the Interior must ensure that in Kosovo and Metohija the organisation is such that all special police detachments are subordinated to the Chief of the Secretariat ..." Was that done, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then beyond that one paragraph it says: "Set up supervisory control with special authorisations within the 124th ... so that they can take very specific measures to keep in check the conduct of the police ..." What do you know about that? In some ways that sounds like the 124th is being tasked to be especially in charge in checking on the conduct of all the rest of the police. Did that happen? Do you know anything about what that's talking about?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, really, this is the first that I see or hear of it so I couldn't really tell you what was meant here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Nobody -- nobody talked to you as brigade commander about doing something like that on or after the 7th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, well I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. If you could go to the very end of the document, I think it's the next-to-the-last bullet point, it talks about members of the reserve police stations. It says: "They may not wear police uniforms, and this has to be prohibited immediately except when they've been engaged according to the plan ..." Up to this point had there been a problem with reserve police officers wearing military uniforms and basically going around acting like they were regular, full-time police officers? Do you know why this was brought up at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I said that I did not attend the meeting, and now I don't know how useful an interpretation that I could give you would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I don't think you had to be at the meeting to be able to help us with this. Right above that bullet point you see it says: "Urgently set up checks of those wearing police uniforms; uniforms may only be worn by members of the police with a 'P' status and the reserve police when it's engaged and no one else. The green uniform may only be worn in anti-terrorist actions ..." So it sounds like before now there's been a problem with people wearing the police uniforms when maybe they weren't supposed to be. Do you have any knowledge or experience about that happening in Kosovo before May 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is a possibility here that some people were observed wearing a uniform at times when they were not in service -- well, our people down there like uniforms, and then they like wearing uniforms even when they shouldn't be wearing uniforms. Sometimes it would happen that a man who was not in the service at all would go to a shop and buy a uniform there. It's not even good that such shops existed. So I can't really see what else this could be, something along those lines, that there were some individuals who were wearing uniforms when they were not in active service. They were wearing uniforms in their villages, in cafes, while -- when they were out drinking, and that's not proper conduct. And this is the only way in which I can actually interpret this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And some of those people who liked to do that and were doing that were also carrying the weapons that had been issued to them; right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Oh, come now, really. The ones who liked to dress up like policemen or wear their police uniforms when they weren't entitled to didn't also like to carry the weapons while they were doing it? Is that what you're telling me?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic, that sounded like cross-examination to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't want to get involved, but I don't really see any mention of weapons in this text. I see uniforms being mentioned and now my learned friend, Mr. Hannis, has come to weapons. I may be mistaken -- well, if I am, then please by all means let us continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, with good humour we've come to the point of correcting you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I appreciate that, and your point is well taken. I apologise. I think it's been two years since I've did direct examination. I've only done cross in the past year or so, so I'm a little rusty. But I take your point, and I will return to the appropriate form of asking the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With the rust well rubbed away I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I hope so, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I'll withdraw that question. Let me take you to the next exhibit which is tab 34 in your binder, and this is Exhibit P345 in evidence. This is a meeting of the MUP staff on the 11th of May, 1999. I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could I tender the last exhibit before I continue to talk about this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 01996 would be assigned P00771, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At this 11 May meeting you're listed specifically by name as having attended. Did you see this document with Mr. Stamp, and can you tell us if you recall having been present for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And I want to ask you in particular about a couple things that you said. If you could go to item number 7; it's where you're listed as speaking. It's on page 4 of the English. I think it's at the bottom of page 3 in yours and the top of page 4. You mentioned some of the operations that you had been involved in, and then on page 4 you mention that morale is high, although the men have been in the woods in the cold and rain for 13 days continually. Is that in connection with the Jezerce operation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I think you told us before that, that was a long and difficult action. Do you recall, were there any SAJ units or reserve SAJ involved in the Jezerce operation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that SAJ took part in the Jezerce operation. I don't know what the composition of their unit was because they were not deployed there with me for me to know that, but I know that SAJ did take part in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You also reported on your relations with the VJ, and you said they are without problems when we communicate with senior VJ officers whom we know well, but then you mentioned a problem with a particular colonel, Jovanovic. Who are the senior VJ officers who you knew well and had good cooperation with from the VJ, if you know? By name.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if I'll be able to remember all of them. Primarily, there was Colonel Cirkovic. I mostly took part in those operations with him. Colonel Jelic, as he was at the time. I don't know if I also was -- participated with Colonel Zivanovic -- well, that would be more or less it. So for the most part I took part with Colonel Cirkovic and Colonel Jelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall now which brigades or VJ units they were with by number and designator?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 15th Armoured Brigade was the unit that was under the command of Colonel Cirkovic. He was colonel at the time, and I think that the 243rd Motorised or Mechanised Brigade - I'm not sure there - was the unit that was under the command of Colonel Jelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that's right. And Zivanovic, was he the 125th?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 125th, but I'm not sure whether I took part in any of the actions with him, but for the other two units I'm absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. A few more questions about some of your colleagues' comments. Number 8, Colonel Prljevic commented, and the next-to-last point he mentioned: "We had to work on some points again with Sigma and Jastreb and defend positions held by others ..." Are Sigma and Jastreb some kind of aeroplanes?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These are call-signs for some of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Oh, okay. And do you know who they referred to or what units they referred to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume that the code-names of the units changed with time, but as far as I can recall at this point in time it appears to me that Sigma was the Novi Sad detachment, the 23rd Detachment, and it seems to me, but with this caveat that I'm not really sure, that Jastreb was the 36th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But don't take my word for it because the names changed at some point in time, so it's possible that the same code-name was used for two different units in two different time-periods.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If you can look at number 10, the 37th PJP Detachment commander, Colonel Mitrovic. And it's the -- I think the sixth bullet point under his name. It's on page 6 of the English. I'm not sure if it's page 4 or 5 for you. Do you see that reference? It says: "The leadership of legija in the final operations was felt, particularly when some equipment was used which helped us a lot." Do you know what "Legija" refers to there? That's the nickname of the JSO commander, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you. It's logical to assume that this is the case, but I'm not sure whether it is a reference to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Numbers 11, 12, and 13 are brigade company commanders. Did you know all those commanders? Were they under you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were the company commanders from Djakovica, Prizren, and Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And number 12, Colic is from Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The last bullet point under his name he talks about the people and refugees in town being treated correctly, but says: " ... however, after all the operations VJ reservists burned houses and went into them; we informed VJ commanders in order to prevent these incidents." Were you aware of that situation in Djakovica before this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Upon learning of this information at the meeting, did you have any obligation to report to anybody about it, or was it any obligation for you to do anything?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an obligation to do anything with this regard. There was the chief of the secretariat in Djakovica, and I suppose that Colic, who was also the chief of the police department, had informed the chief of the secretariat, and he, in turn, informed the army unit. The fact that he was the commander of the company does not mean that he was subordinated to me but to his superior in the secretariat when it came to his regular duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to number 13, Krsto Djurcic. Number 2, the bullet point number 2 he says: "We did not have any losses except for Salipur who was killed while undertaking measures without our approval." Do you know who Salipur was?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a police officer affiliated with the secretariat in Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know him personally? Did you ever meet him before he died?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name rings a bell, but I never spoke to him. I knew him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can I show you a photograph, then, that is 65 ter number 03111. We'll put it up on the screen. I don't have it in your binder. Do you have the picture on your monitor now?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you recognise any of the people in that photograph; and if so, can you tell us where they are situated and who they are?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side or going from the right-hand side, I believe that I can see the policeman sitting down at the far right. I believe that his family name is Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Left to him is Goran Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who was he?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time he was the assistant commander of the MUP staff in Pristina, at the time when he was in Kosmet, I mean. I don't know the other two. The one standing on the left with receding hair is Mileta Novakovic. To the right of him, I can't see too well. It could be Salipur, but I'm really not sure. It would have to be blown up a little. I didn't know him that well. It does look like him, though. I believe that he was a bit heavier than depicted in this photo, more heavily built. It looks like him, but I can't be sure. And the man at the very right of the photo, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what unit these men were associated with in 1998 and/or 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Were they special -- were they PJP at any time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but I know that in 1999 he was -- I don't know whether he was before that; it is possible. I don't know these people. I don't know these members.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But apparently Salipur was a PJP because he's reported on by the company commander as having been killed.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that he was in 1999. And in the minutes you can see that this was indeed the case if my interpretation is correct. Whether he was there before that, I don't know. By the logic of the matter, it would be really unrealistic for me to know everybody. I knew some officers, some other people that I'd known before, but there were simply too many people for me to know everybody. It would be unrealistic to expect that from me. I can't tell you exactly who was where and when. There is a strong possibility that he was there. I mean, it's obvious that he was there in 1999. It's pretty clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of a group called Munja, a unit called Munja, in Pec in 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What can you tell us about that? When did you hear about it? What did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you when I heard of them first; however, from what I did hear it was composed of police members, and their task was to carry out some more complex tasks in 1998, if I'm not mistaken, in the very town. This could have been sometime in mid-1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know who created this special unit?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe that they were composed of police members, or at least that was my impression. I really can't talk in any more detail because I just have a vague idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It -- but it's unusual, isn't it, for a police unit to be called Munja? Wouldn't it have a designation like a PJP detachment or a police company from Pec SUP? Am I misunderstanding it? What kind of unit is this? Is this an operational sweep group with a nickname? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, if somebody wants to call themselves Munja, it's an internal name. It's not an official name of any unit. For example, there is a platoon that want to call themselves Dusan [indiscernible]. I don't know; it's something that doesn't say anything in principle. That was not an official name, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. At one of the meetings we talked about earlier, the 17 February 1999 meeting in Exhibit P85, the last -- one of the last things said by Mr. Stojiljkovic at that meeting, if you could look at tab 32 for just a second. On the last page, the second bullet point from the bottom, the minister says: "Raise discipline, behaviour, and appearance of policemen to a high level. Do away with Rambo-style caps and bandannas ..." Isn't that related to the kinds of problems that are associated with a police group calling itself Munja? Isn't that the same kind of problem? Is there a lack of discipline if you start going around and wearing other than official police gear and calling yourselves by special names like "Lightning" or "Munja," wasn't that a problem within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was, it was a marginal problem. I suppose that there were individuals who decided to wear hats or bandannas, but it was not a widespread phenomenon, and you can see that in what you have just read.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender the photograph, 3111.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00772, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe somebody knows people in this photo, but I don't know who it is. The witness did say whom he recognised, but nobody actually told us who the people are. I don't know whether you are aware of somebody having done that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I've heard several names listed from the evidence, and I believe the witness himself was second from the right in the front, but that is yet to be confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll clear that up, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we can go back to the photograph, I think, if I read the transcript right, you told us the person on the front row, second from the right, was Guri Radosavljevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all good and well -- can we just have the identification of the persons to see who's standing, who is in the photo. The witness said, I believe that this is so and so, but why can't we see the caption under the photo to see who actually is in the photo? Does that exist or not? I don't know whether I'm making myself clear. The witness described everything. He says, I think this is so and so, but nobody ever confirmed to us the true names and who these people are. I want to know the origin of the photo, the chain of custody, and how the identity of the persons in the photo was established irrespective of what a witness has to tell us about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, Mr. Djurdjic, we're not going to spend time going into all of that. The witness identified some of the people in this photograph, and the Prosecution sees the photograph as relevant to its case, so it will be received. But you are clearing up the identity of one person, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know if you answered that. Can you tell us who the person is who's second from the right on the front row in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Second from the right on the front row.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the middle there are three people there --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, in the front row the people kneeling, second from the right.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second from the right looks like Goran Radosavljevic to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you told us he was a deputy on the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was at the time an assistant to the commander in the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General Sreten Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: His nickname is Guri; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think the witness did indicate where the other people were in the photograph in terms of their position, so I'm satisfied that we know who's who and where they are to the best of his ability. With that, Your Honours, I don't have any further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Djurdjic, do you cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I did not realise that Mr. Hannis had completed his examination-in-chief. Yes, I will cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Brakovic. The Defence team of the accused, General Djordjevic, consists of Ms. Marie O'Leary, my legal assistant; and myself, Veljko Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I hope you're in good health and that we can continue, you're feeling well?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Be my guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, before I proceed and start putting my questions to you, since we're speaking the same language, in order to facilitate the work of the people who interpret and are in charge of the transcript, please speak slowly and wait for my question to be interpreted before you start providing your answer. If we proceed in that way, everything will be okay.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It seems that Mr. Stamp has forgotten to provide Mr. Hannis with the notes -- the proofing notes from your proofing session on the 3rd of May, 2009, with regard to the corrections of the statement that was previously provided by yourself. In your binder you have your statement. Could you please go to that statement. That was a statement that you provided in 2004. And in the notes provided to me by Mr. Stamp, P7P9 [as interpreted] is the statement number. It says that Mr. Brakovic wanted to clarify paragraph 26. Could you please look at the paragraph, read it for yourself, and could you please tell us after that what is it that you wanted to clarify?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 26?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that General Vlastimir Djordjevic and Obrad Stevanovic, assistant minister, during 1999 regularly visited Kosovo. I don't know any concrete details with regard to their roles in Kosovo, but I assume that they were there to check the situation and carry out their regular duties in keeping with their positions. I'm not sure whether Dragan Ilic was ever in Kosovo or what his role could be over there. In a conversation that I had at the request of the Tribunal in Pristina -- or rather, I apologise, in Belgrade in the special prosecutor's office, there was a lot of insistence on this paragraph. They asked me to explain who was in Kosovo and when. I suggested that Mr. Stamp and I look at it and he did not object to that, but I believe that this would be a topic of my examination yesterday and here today and that there will be plenty of opportunities to provide further explanations, and that's what my request was about. Would you like me to go over that paragraph again and tell you what I actually meant? The fact is that Generals Vlastimir Djordjevic and Obrad Stevanovic did frequently visit Kosovo. My position at the time - and you could draw your conclusion as to what it was, I was the chief of the department of the police and the commander of the 124th Intervention Brigade - I could see the generals either in the field or at various meetings. And in that sense I said that I saw them very frequently because at every meeting I attended was attended by one of them. As we went through all the meetings just a little while ago, we saw who was there and at what time. So you can actually draw your own conclusions as to who was in Kosovo and when. As for my seeing them in the field, I have to say that I saw General Obrad Stevanovic several times. Sometime at the beginning of the war when the post office in Pristina was bombarded, he was present there, I was present there, we were trying to save some civilians who were stranded in their homes. And during the anti-terrorist operations, during the period after that, I didn't see either General Djordjevic or General Obrad Stevanovic, which means that in that sense I said what I did upon the insistence during the interview in Belgrade. And in that sense, I, bearing in mind that there was a lot of insistence upon that, I thought that I was speaking in general terms, and I wanted to clarify what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brakovic. Is it true what I'm reading now under item 10? You said that you saw General Vlastimir Djordjevic on the 10th of June in Pristina after the signing of the Kumanovo Agreement at the ministerial meeting there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that General Djordjevic was at the meeting in Pristina upon the signing of the Kumanovo Agreement, and the meeting was about the implementation of the agreement in the upcoming period, and for that reason I believe that he was present, if I'm not mistaken, if my memory serves me right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I have a request. I don't know whether this would be a good time for a technical break, or maybe you would like to use the five remaining minutes and then make a break. It would suit me to have a break now in order to continue my cross-examination after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will take the second break now, Mr. Djurdjic, to assist you, and we will resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like the Court Deputy to put on our screens P57.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, I would like to ask you if you find that easier to look at the decision establishing the ministry staff of the 16th of June, 1996 -- 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if somebody could tell me which document that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now -- can you see it now on your screen?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I immediately started making mistakes. I will try and make pauses as much as I can. Mr. Hannis showed you this decision of the 16th of June, 1998. It was issued by the Minister of the Interior, Mr. Stojiljkovic, and you told us that you knew David Gajic. Could you please tell me where did Mr. Gajic work, in what department of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. David Gajic, the late Mr. David Gajic, worked in the state security department as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I right that Mr. David Gajic was appointed the deputy head of the staff, the head being General Sreten Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here in this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like us to look at the other assistant for special operations, is this Milorad Lukovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was Mr. Milorad Lukovic's function and what part of the MUP did he work at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he worked in the state security department, I think, as a commander of the unit for special operations, JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brakovic. As for Mr. Zivko Trajkovic, we've already noted that he was the assistant for special anti-terrorist units, SAJs, and can you tell us what function he had in addition to his function in the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know he was the commander of the special anti-terrorist unit, the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we now move to page 2 -- or just in the Serbian version. You can leave the English version where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right if I say that after the personnel decisions, the appointments as outlined here in this decision, the members of the staff in its extended compositions include also the chiefs of the secretariats of the interior, the RDB departments in the AP Kosovo and Metohija, the autonomous province?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that's what it says here in this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brakovic, as a long-time employee in the MUP, is it true that members of one department cannot issue tasks to personnel in the other department within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that the personnel - let me give you an example - in the public security department cannot assign tasks to the personnel in the state security department and vice versa in regular work?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right, it is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I right that the minister of the interior does have the right in light of the fact that he is in charge of both the public and state security departments to set up some bodies that would involve personnel from both departments?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does have this discretionary power.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the decision that we are looking at now, does it cover both personnel of the state security department and of the public security department?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of what we've seen, that would be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to this decision, is General Sreten Lukic appointed the head of the staff and he was in the public security department?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And his deputy is a man who belonged to the state security department, Mr. Gajic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Brakovic, I would like us to look at Roman numeral II in this decision, it's on the same page in the Serbian version, and in the English version we remain on the same page too. Am I right, Mr. Brakovic, that this decision of the minister tasks the staff with planning, organising, and leading the work of the organisational units of the ministry and any units seconded or attached to it in suppressing terrorism in the territory of the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this item, the staff is also authorised to carry out more complex special security tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we move on to page 3. Could we please have --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 2 of the English version. You can keep the B/C/S version on the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, in this decision the minister decided, did he not, that for his work, the work of the staff, and the security situation within the framework of the work of the staff the head of the staff shall be responsible only to him, to the minister?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that the minister ordered that the head of the staff should inform him about any security incidents, any measures taken, and the results of those measures?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to move to the last page of this decision in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, could you please look at paragraph 6. Mr. Hannis discussed it at length with you yesterday. And could you please look at the decisions 1206/98 of the 15th of May, 1998, and this decision of 1206 of the 12th of June, 1998. Now I want to ask you whether I'm correct that all those decisions that are listed here in paragraph 6 are no longer valid as of the entry into force of this decision?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says here, with the coming into force of this decision the following shall cease to be valid and that includes the documents that you listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 1 of both of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right that the minister by this decision establishes a staff for the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia to suppress terrorism in the territory of the AP of Kosovo and Metohija, that this was the name of the staff as it is indicated at paragraph 1 of this decision?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask -- I would like to ask the Court Deputy to put on our screens Exhibit D001-6229.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for this document to come up on our screens, Mr. Brakovic, do you know Major-General Momcilo Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was appointed a member of the staff of the MUP in Pristina in 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the staff, but I don't know -- well, he's not listed here in the decision, but he was on the staff. He did take care of some tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, do you see this decision, the one that you can see here in Serbo-Croatian, it's dated the 2nd of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that this is a decision to appoint a member of the ministry staff for the suppression of terrorism, Mr. -- that's Major-General Momcilo Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, with the tasks that I don't want to go into now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 2 of this decision in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, in paragraph marked with the Roman numeral III, am I correct if I say that the minister decided that General Stojanovic should be responsible for his work to the head of the staff and the minister?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00099, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I would like to ask the Court Deputy if we could have on our screens document -- it's a 65 ter 0448. I apologise, I may have misspoken, 65 ter 4478.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, did you know Mr. Dragan Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that he was also, or rather, did you know that he was also a member of the MUP staff for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija for a while?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This decision of the 21st of May, 1999, is this a decision to appoint deputy head of the ministry staff for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija and the person appointed here is Mr. Dragan Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 2 of this document, or rather -- yes, that is the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, who issued this decision?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Vlajko Stojiljkovic. Thank you, Mr. Brakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this decision that we're looking at now was issued -- is this -- I'm sorry, is this P259 -- yes, I do apologise, it's already admitted into evidence. It's an exhibit and the number is P259 so I don't have to tender it, and I apologise. Could we please have document, it's a 65 ter document, 01251.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, I'm right if I say that you're not familiar with this decision?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the decision that we looked at yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No. The decision that we looked at yesterday follows after this, but this decision was not shown to you yesterday. Mr. Brakovic, that's why I told you to look in particular at the end of the 16th of June decision. This is the decision number 1206/98 which was invalidated by the decision. And am I right if I say that this is the decision on the formation of the staff of the ministry in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay, let's take it one thing at a time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The counsel and witness are kindly asked to make pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You heard that request, Mr. Djurdjic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm doing my best, but it seems that it's not good enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right when I say that paragraph 2 of this decision establishing the staff of the ministry in Pristina stipulates that it should plan, organise, and direct the work of the Secretariats of the Interior and the border police stations in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija in the execution of more complex and major tasks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now we have A, B, V -- A, B, C, D. Now it says suppression of civil unrest, terrorism, and armed insurgency. Am I right that this element that is listed under A is the reason why the PJP units could be engaged in accordance with the decision that we saw yesterday that Mr. Hannis showed you about 124th Intervention Brigade, that this was the legal basis?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The wording in subparagraph A, so major and more complex tasks that are listed here under A, B, C, and so on, under A we have suppression of civil unrest, terrorism, and armed rebellion. Now I'm asking you is this, what we see here under A, the basis for the establishment of the 124th Brigade stemming from the decision to establish PJPs for the engagement of the PJPs on specific tasks? This is the decision that we saw yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we move on, and I wouldn't go quoting everything from this decision, and we see here under 4, am I right, that the composition of the staff, the head of the staff and its members shall be decided by a special decision? And I'm now interested in item 5. Am I right, that for their work, the work of the staff and situation of security within the purview of the staff in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, the head of the staff shall be responsible to the chief of the sector for security?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to the following page. And in the English version as well, can I ask for the following page to be put on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you now repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, item number 5.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The staff leader is responsible to the chief of the public security department for his own work, the work of the staff, and the state of public security. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And under 6 the staff leader informs the chief of the public security.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that this decision was issued on the 15th of May, 1998, and that it was signed by Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic, the assistant minister?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At that time he was also the chief of the public security department; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document please be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And what would be assigned D00100, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to go back to Exhibit P -- P760 or P6760 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We admitted the document yesterday. It is the decision that we talked about where the date, the 12th of June, was not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, Mr. Hannis showed you this decision, did he not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you please look at the personnel composition in this decision who were the members of the staff, General Lukic, wasn't he, as the head?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Then there's Mr. Djinovic as a deputy?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Goran Radosavljevic follows?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then you, yourself, Mr. Vukovic, and so on and so forth until the very end. And now I would kindly ask you to look at the following page of this decision. Mr. Brakovic, please look at the decision and tell me if I'm right in thinking that all the appointed persons who are members of the department of public security.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There's no single person from the state security department?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brakovic. And now could you please look at the Roman II. Does this paragraph -- appoints the chiefs of the secretariats of the interior in the territory of the AP Kosovo and Metohija as members of the expanded staff?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you agree with me that the minister annulled the decision that was passed on the 16th of June and another decision passed by the chief of the [indiscernible], both the one passed in May and June?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true; that's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you agree with me, or let's affirm that the decision that was issued by the minister, he encompassed members of both departments or the SUP chiefs in Kosovo and Metohija and chiefs of the centres and departments of the state security?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Brakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would kindly ask the court to produce 01507, this is a 65 ter document. We already have a number, it's P58, which means that it has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right in thinking that this is a decision on the establishment of special police units?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you now please tell me under item 2 of this decision what are the tasks and duties of the special police units?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read that from the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Go on then.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The tasks and duties of the PJM are to perform as necessary certain duties falling within the responsibility of the Ministry of the Interior ... relating to the protection of the security of the republic and its citizens."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Brakovic. I want to ask you this: The origins of the special units of the police, did they exist already after the insurgence of Ustasha terrorists on Mount Radusa in 1972 the PJMs were not established after the events on Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, from various books that I have perused, that statement of yours would be correct. After Radusa there were efforts in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And we're also going to see later on when this decision was issued. Am I right in saying, Mr. Brakovic, that under paragraph 2 of item 2, it is prescribed that bringing into readiness, mobilising, and engaging the PJM on performing tasks defined in paragraph 1 of this item shall be done on orders from the minister ..."

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And when approved by the minister, Mr. Brakovic, this can also be done by the chief of the public security department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right in saying that the chief of department is not authorised to independently issue a decision on bringing into readiness, mobilising, and engaging the PJMs?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a lawyer by profession, but as I'm interpreting this item I believe that you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Brakovic. Mr. Brakovic am I right in saying the following, members of the PJMs will remain deployed and will perform tasks during the time when they're not engaged as members of the PJM, and they are entitled to the rights stemming from their employment in keeping with the decision on their deployment?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that the PJPs were established as the MUP forces to carry out special security tasks which are relative to the protection of the security of the republic and its citizens?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we have already established that just a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that - and I'm drawing conclusions - that the maintenance of public order and security relates to public gatherings?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Establishing public law and order when this has been impaired to a large extent?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Deprivation of freedom of hardened criminals?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Detection, capturing, and destruction of insurgents and insurgent groups and others, sabotage and terrorist groups and individuals?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And whenever the interests of public law and order of the republic and its citizens so demand, including combat tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm interested in one thing, and I would move to the topic of the operational sweep groups. What is the official title operational sweep group or operational pursuit group?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I understand this term is the operational sweep group.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sweep group. Okay. Am I right in saying that within the framework of every company of a PJP, one unit was established of the members who were the fittest and the most capable, and they represented that operational sweep group?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from all the detachments?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then they underwent special training in order to attain the necessary level of capabilities?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me just go back to one thing. Am I right in saying that the tasks of the PJP applied to the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm reading in the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that when in the same area or on the same task there are several units intervening and belonging to a PJP, the unification of the function of command, control, and coordination is regulated by a special order?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what situation are you referring to. Are you talking in general terms, or are you talking about the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Not in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. I'm going to give you an example. We're talking about demonstrations in 1996 and 1997 in Belgrade, for example.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Units were sent there to intervene during the demonstrations in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And what's your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that an order as to be issued in order to establish - since the men come from different units - who would be in command of all those units?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that that would be the case, but as I've already said, this went beyond my level.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Have you ever been to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that those units were commanded by the chief of the SUP of the city of Belgrade to whom the units were addressed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying - and now we're talking about the years 1998 and 1999 - that the MUP staff in order to suppress terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija commanded all the units addressed and subordinated to them pursuant to the decision of the minister dated 16 June 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the -- arises from the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that the planning of anti-terrorist actions on -- came in 1998 and 1999 was done by the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the plans in question which were drafted by the army you received via the MUP staff for the suppression of terrorism on Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one of the answers I already said that partly yes and partly those plans went directly, so I suppose that everything went through the staff at the end of the day. There were periods when we received those through the secretariat, but I believe that that also went through the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that the administrative and logistics tasks with regard to the training, equipping, and sending of the PJP units was carried out by the administration of the ministry police?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that in the course of 1998 and 1999 via the MUP staff in Pristina there were efforts to supply, equip, and everything else that was necessary for the work of the PJP units in Kosovo with regard to the police administration in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question. It was not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The MUP staff in Pristina in 1998 and 1999, did they submit to the police administration their request for the supply of equipment and all the other necessary means for all units that were deployed on Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that you are right, but I was not in a position to know that. I never dealt with that, but I suppose that was the case because it could only be logical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Brakovic, when you look at the decision that we have in front of us on the establishment of the PJPs of the police --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Exhibit P257.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In essence the contents of this decision establishing the 124th Intervention Brigade in addition to it being mentioned in here, in all other aspects is it identical with the decision to establish the special units of the milicija that we've seen just a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that I answered this question yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that all the accompanying documents are the ones that are envisaged in the decision establishing the PJMs of the milicija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this is something that we said yesterday, that the decision to establish the 124th Brigade was issued by minister of the interior. Do you agree that the dispatch sent by the chief of the department with this decision establishing the PJP in its attachment was instructive in its character? It was just by way of information, notification?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that. So please find attached a decision and it is specified that there are some obligations pertaining to record-keeping. I don't think -- well, it's not up on the screen. I can't really remember all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Lets clear one thing up. I think that it has to be cleared up. When you were appointed the commander of the 124th Intervention Brigade, or rather, when you were doing that job, you were not doing the job of the chief of the department of the interior in the Secretariat of the Interior in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It was my deputy who did that job.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And when you were doing your job as commander of the 124th Brigade, the chief of the SUP was not our superior?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And while you did the job of the commander you did not submit reports to the SUP chief?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Except, unfortunately, if there are any injuries or casualties of any sort, then you have to inform the secretariat, the original secretariat, from which the casualty -- where the casualty worked?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we called that informing or notification, not reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Notification and not reporting. Thank you. Am I right, or rather, I am right because I already asked this question. We can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at P537 -- P357. Just a moment. Let me check. No, I do apologise, my error. It's P75.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, this is a decision appointing Mr. Bosko Petric as the chief of the SUP in Pristina; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And we can see the date is the 4th of June, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could scroll up a little bit -- scroll down, please, so that we can see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that the decision was issued by minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, yes, although the Serbian version is a little bit dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you can look at the English version, it's much clearer there.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So let's clear this up. We can see that -- well, there was an exhibit that pertained to telephones where Mr. Djoka [as interpreted] Keric was mentioned. So this was before Mr. Petric came to be the chief, and we can see that it was in 1997. So it predates that period; is that correct, Mr. Brakovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that when the Prosecutor asked me that, that's what I responded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but now we know for sure. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm about to embark on a new topic, and our time is running out. I think it would be appropriate for me to end now for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Djurdjic. We will adjourn now, and we resume on Monday -- I believe it will be in the morning of Monday at 9.00. I'm afraid, Mr. Brakovic, we must ask you to return again on Monday. As you can readily see, your evidence is not concluded. The court officer will make arrangements with you for your continued stay, and we continue your evidence on Monday. We now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 11th day of May, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
